close_reason: extract_account_id now validates accountId against RFC 8620 §1.2 via Id::new_validated (already available in jmap-types). Malformed inputs — empty strings, strings containing forbidden ASCII characters like SPACE or DQUOTE, strings exceeding 255 bytes — now surface as invalidArguments with the validation error message, instead of silently passing through to the backend's account_exists call as either notFound or storage-layer parse errors. Added two helpers tests: one asserts each of the four documented rejection cases produces invalidArguments, the other asserts a well-formed Id passes and the rest of the args are returned intact.
description:
Scenario: a JMAP client sends {"accountId": ""} or {"accountId": "a/b"} or a 1000-char string. crate-jmap-server/src/helpers.rs:42-48 does match args.get("accountId").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) → Some(s) → Id::from(s). No length check, no character-set check. The Id wraps the string and flows through to backend.account_exists(caller, &id), where the backend now has to decide: 404 (not found), 400 (invalid), or crash on storage-layer name validation.

RFC 8620 §1.2 specifies Id as a string of 1-255 chars from [A-Za-z0-9_-]. Anything outside that grammar cannot be a valid JMAP Id by spec. A handler that accepts an empty Id and forwards it to the backend either:
- gets a synthetic notFound from the backend (most likely — fine but lossy: client doesn't learn the Id is malformed, just that it doesn't exist)
- triggers a downstream parse error inside the backend with bookkeeping (worst case: SQL parameter binding, S3 key composition, etc.)

This is pre-existing behaviour — the diff just touched extract_account_id's signature, not its validation. But the function is now the single ingress point for accountId on every generic handler, so adding RFC-grade validation here pays out across every *-server. The right shape is probably to add fn Id::try_from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, JmapError> to jmap-types, then have extract_account_id call it and surface invalidArguments on mismatch.

Maintenance consequence: an issue report 'why does Foo/get return notFound for accountId="my account"' that turns out to be the space character. The fix surfaces as 'invalidArguments: accountId is not a valid Id (RFC 8620 §1.2)' — actionable, not a CVE — but the absent validation is a recurring class of bug report waiting to happen, especially as more *-server crates onboard.

Workspace scope: bump jmap-types to add the validator before changing the helper, then the helper change is one line.
title: extract_account_id does not validate Id wire format (RFC 8620 §1.2)
